liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Sugaree follows Not Fade Away and comes right before Wang Dang Doodle; Jerry plays subtle inflections on Sugaree [10][14]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Phil and Brent play a jazzy jam leading into Drums after a well-bent Terrapin Station [9]
- **Beer Barrel Polka' tuning** (1 review): Brent plays an orchestral passage during roughly three minutes of tuning; Jerry announces the first of the night's technical difficulties [11]
- **Beer Barrel Polka** (1 review): The band plays Beer Barrel Polka to fill time, then two drum slams launch straight into Not Fade Away [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-02-06d1t01**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd89-02-06d1t02**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd89-02-06d1t03**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd89-02-06d1t04**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd89-02-06d1t05**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd89-02-06d1t06**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd89-02-06d1t07**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd89-02-06d1t08**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd89-02-06.sbd.miller-walker-scotton.26330.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 144 min; rated 3.82/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Good vocal harmonies; every instrument is present, including a clearly audible Bobby, and Phil's bass is strong; Reviewer reports great sound quality on the Charlie Miller soundboard transfer [14][15]
- **gd1989-02-06.sbd.walker.scotton-miller.107030.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 145 min; rated 3/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard recording great, though the tracks are mislabeled [19]
- **gd1989-02-06.147384.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 148 min [4]
- **gd1989-02-06.146587.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 148 min [5]
- **gd1989-02-06.ec7.bowen.116443.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 139 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [6]
- **gd89-02-06.sennheiser-fob.wiley.9485.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 19 songs; 139 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this Sennheiser audience copy to have very poor sound quality [12]

## Around the show

- Taper first saw the Dead at Kaiser on February 9, 1986, and loved the venue [17]
- Reviewer says the sound is even better than the previous night's show, which also sounded good [9]
- Reviewer calls it a decent show, but says the previous night was a bit better [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd89-02-06.sbd.miller-walker-scotton.26330.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard to master cassette to CD (Marantz CDR 500 Pro), then transferred via Sony CDP-XE500, Behringer SRC2000, and Cool Edit to FLAC; Charlie Miller transferred and edited it, with thanks to Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [1]
- **gd1989-02-06.sbd.walker.scotton-miller.107030.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell MX90/Dolby B) [3]
- **gd1989-02-06.147384.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [4]. Also: Made from a cassette master using AT835B and AT8202 microphones, transferred and mastered by Charlie Miller; patch source recorded by M. Laurentus [4]
- **gd1989-02-06.146587.sbd.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [5]. Also: Cassette master from AT835B and AT8202 mics, mastered by Charlie Miller, with a patch source recorded by M. Laurentus [5]
- **gd1989-02-06.ec7.bowen.116443.flac16**: taped by Jeff Bowen; transferred by Brad Foster; source: Source: (OTS) Superscope EC-7's (ortf/cardioids) > Sony WM-D6C; [6]. Also: Taper used Superscope EC-7 microphones; these were the last shows he recorded with them [17]
- **gd89-02-06.sennheiser-fob.wiley.9485.sbeok.shnf**: source: Mark Horvath FOB Senn. 421Âs> Sony TC-D5> MC> CDR [7]. Also: Mark Horvath recorded with front-of-board Sennheiser 421s into a Sony TC-D5, then cassette to CDR; seeded to Etree by Tim W [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center - February 7, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/february-7-1989) [22]
